$comment: The BigQuery functions the editor explains. Edit this file, then run `just bigquery-snippets` to write bigquery-functions.code-snippets.json. See snippets/README.md.

functions.name: CURRENT_DATE
functions.doc: Returns today's date, in the given time zone or UTC.

params.name: time_zone
params.doc: a time zone name such as 'Europe/London', or an offset such as '+01:00'

functions.name: DATE
functions.doc: Makes a DATE from its parts, or takes the date of a TIMESTAMP or DATETIME.

params.name: time_zone
params.doc: a time zone name such as 'Europe/London', or an offset such as '+01:00'

functions.name: DATE_ADD
functions.doc: Adds a number of days, weeks, months, quarters or years to a date.

params.name: interval
params.doc: `INTERVAL n part`, e.g. `INTERVAL 7 DAY`; part is DAY, WEEK, MONTH, QUARTER or YEAR

functions.name: DATE_SUB
functions.doc: Subtracts a number of days, weeks, months, quarters or years from a date.

params.name: interval
params.doc: `INTERVAL n part`, e.g. `INTERVAL 7 DAY`; part is DAY, WEEK, MONTH, QUARTER or YEAR

functions.name: DATE_DIFF
functions.doc: Returns the number of `granularity` boundaries between two dates: `end_date` minus `start_date`.

functions.name: DATE_TRUNC
functions.doc: Truncates a date to the start of the given granularity.

params.name: time_zone
params.doc: a time zone name such as 'Europe/London', or an offset such as '+01:00'

notes: `WEEK` weeks start on Sunday; `WEEK(MONDAY)` (or any weekday) starts them on that day, and `ISOWEEK` on Monday.

functions.name: FORMAT_DATE
functions.doc: Formats a date as a string, by format elements.

params.name: format_string
params.doc: format elements such as '%Y-%m-%d'; see the docs for every element

functions.name: PARSE_DATE
functions.doc: Reads a DATE from a string, by format elements. The whole string must match the format.

params.name: format_string
params.doc: format elements such as '%Y-%m-%d'; see the docs for every element

functions.name: LAST_DAY
functions.doc: Returns the last day of the month, or of the given period, that holds the date.

params.name: date_part
params.doc: MONTH when left out

functions.name: EXTRACT
functions.doc: Returns one part of a date, datetime, time or timestamp.

params.name: time_zone
params.doc: for a TIMESTAMP: the time zone to read it in, UTC when left out

signatures.returns: INT64 (DATE, DATETIME or TIME for those parts)

functions.name: GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY
functions.doc: Returns an array of dates from `start_date` to `end_date`, both included, a step apart.

params.name: interval
params.doc: `INTERVAL n part`; part is DAY, WEEK, MONTH, QUARTER or YEAR. One day when left out

notes: Use it with `UNNEST` to make one row for each date: `SELECT day FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY(...)) AS day`.

functions.name: CURRENT_DATETIME
functions.doc: Returns the date and time now, in the given time zone or UTC, with no time zone kept.

params.name: time_zone
params.doc: a time zone name such as 'Europe/London', or an offset such as '+01:00'

functions.name: DATETIME
functions.doc: Makes a DATETIME from its parts, from a DATE and a TIME, or from a TIMESTAMP in a time zone.

params.name: time_zone
params.doc: a time zone name such as 'Europe/London', or an offset such as '+01:00'

params.name: time_expr
params.doc: midnight when left out

functions.name: DATETIME_ADD
functions.doc: Adds an interval to a datetime.

params.name: interval
params.doc: `INTERVAL n part`, e.g. `INTERVAL 2 HOUR`; part is MICROSECOND to YEAR

functions.name: DATETIME_SUB
functions.doc: Subtracts an interval from a datetime.

params.name: interval
params.doc: `INTERVAL n part`, e.g. `INTERVAL 2 HOUR`; part is MICROSECOND to YEAR

functions.name: DATETIME_DIFF
functions.doc: Returns the number of `granularity` boundaries between two datetimes: `end_datetime` minus `start_datetime`.

functions.name: DATETIME_TRUNC
functions.doc: Truncates a datetime to the start of the given granularity.

params.name: time_zone
params.doc: a time zone name such as 'Europe/London', or an offset such as '+01:00'

functions.name: FORMAT_DATETIME
functions.doc: Formats a datetime as a string, by format elements.

params.name: format_string
params.doc: format elements such as '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'

functions.name: PARSE_DATETIME
functions.doc: Reads a DATETIME from a string, by format elements. The whole string must match the format.

params.name: format_string
params.doc: format elements such as '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'

functions.name: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
functions.doc: Returns the time now, as a TIMESTAMP.

functions.name: TIMESTAMP
functions.doc: Makes a TIMESTAMP from a string, a date or a datetime, read in the given time zone or UTC.

params.name: time_zone
params.doc: a time zone name such as 'Europe/London', or an offset such as '+01:00'

functions.name: TIMESTAMP_ADD
functions.doc: Adds an interval to a timestamp.

params.name: interval
params.doc: `INTERVAL n part`, e.g. `INTERVAL 30 MINUTE`; part is MICROSECOND to DAY

functions.name: TIMESTAMP_SUB
functions.doc: Subtracts an interval from a timestamp.

params.name: interval
params.doc: `INTERVAL n part`, e.g. `INTERVAL 30 MINUTE`; part is MICROSECOND to DAY

functions.name: TIMESTAMP_DIFF
functions.doc: Returns the number of whole `granularity` intervals between two timestamps: `end_timestamp` minus `start_timestamp`.

functions.name: TIMESTAMP_TRUNC
functions.doc: Truncates a timestamp to the start of the given granularity, in the given time zone or UTC.

params.name: time_zone
params.doc: a time zone name such as 'Europe/London', or an offset such as '+01:00'

functions.name: FORMAT_TIMESTAMP
functions.doc: Formats a timestamp as a string, by format elements, in the given time zone or UTC.

params.name: format_string
params.doc: format elements such as '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z'

params.name: time_zone
params.doc: a time zone name such as 'Europe/London', or an offset such as '+01:00'

functions.name: PARSE_TIMESTAMP
functions.doc: Reads a TIMESTAMP from a string, by format elements, in the given time zone or UTC.

params.name: format_string
params.doc: format elements such as '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'

params.name: time_zone
params.doc: a time zone name such as 'Europe/London', or an offset such as '+01:00'

functions.name: UNIX_SECONDS
functions.doc: Returns the number of seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC.

functions.name: UNIX_MILLIS
functions.doc: Returns the number of milliseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC.

functions.name: TIMESTAMP_SECONDS
functions.doc: Reads a number of seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC as a TIMESTAMP.

functions.name: TIMESTAMP_MILLIS
functions.doc: Reads a number of milliseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC as a TIMESTAMP.

functions.name: GENERATE_TIMESTAMP_ARRAY
functions.doc: Returns an array of timestamps from `start_timestamp` to `end_timestamp`, both included, an interval apart.

params.name: interval
params.doc: `INTERVAL n part`, e.g. `INTERVAL 1 HOUR`; part is MICROSECOND to DAY

functions.name: CONCAT
functions.doc: Joins values into one. Returns NULL if any value is NULL.

functions.name: LENGTH
functions.doc: Returns the length of a value: characters for a STRING, bytes for BYTES.

functions.name: LOWER
functions.doc: Returns the value in lower case.

functions.name: UPPER
functions.doc: Returns the value in upper case.

functions.name: INITCAP
functions.doc: Upper-cases the first character of each word and lower-cases the rest.

params.name: delimiters
params.doc: the characters that separate words; whitespace and most punctuation when left out

functions.name: TRIM
functions.doc: Removes whitespace, or the given characters, from both ends of a value.

params.name: set_of_characters_to_remove
params.doc: whitespace when left out

functions.name: LTRIM
functions.doc: Removes whitespace, or the given characters, from the start of a value.

params.name: set_of_characters_to_remove
params.doc: whitespace when left out

functions.name: RTRIM
functions.doc: Removes whitespace, or the given characters, from the end of a value.

params.name: set_of_characters_to_remove
params.doc: whitespace when left out

functions.name: SUBSTR
functions.doc: Returns the part of a value that starts at `position` and is `length` long.

params.name: position
params.doc: 1 is the first character; a negative number counts from the end

params.name: length
params.doc: to the end when left out

functions.name: REPLACE
functions.doc: Replaces every occurrence of `from_pattern` with `to_pattern`. Matches exact text, not a regular expression.

functions.name: SPLIT
functions.doc: Splits a value at each delimiter into an array.

params.name: delimiter
params.doc: ',' when left out

functions.name: STARTS_WITH
functions.doc: Whether a value starts with `prefix`.

functions.name: ENDS_WITH
functions.doc: Whether a value ends with `suffix`.

functions.name: CONTAINS_SUBSTR
functions.doc: Whether `search_value` is in `expression`, ignoring case. The expression can also be a STRUCT, an ARRAY or JSON, searched in every field.

params.name: search_value
params.doc: a literal string

functions.name: STRPOS
functions.doc: Returns the 1-based position of the first `subvalue` in `value`, or 0 if it is not found.

functions.name: INSTR
functions.doc: Returns the 1-based position of an occurrence of `search_value`, or 0 if it is not found.

params.name: position
params.doc: where to start; a negative number searches back from the end. 1 when left out

params.name: occurrence
params.doc: which occurrence to find. 1 when left out

functions.name: LPAD
functions.doc: Pads the start of a value with `pattern` until it is `return_length` long.

params.name: pattern
params.doc: a space when left out

functions.name: RPAD
functions.doc: Pads the end of a value with `pattern` until it is `return_length` long.

params.name: pattern
params.doc: a space when left out

functions.name: LEFT
functions.doc: Returns the first `length` characters, or bytes, of a value.

functions.name: RIGHT
functions.doc: Returns the last `length` characters, or bytes, of a value.

functions.name: REPEAT
functions.doc: Returns a value repeated a number of times.

functions.name: REVERSE
functions.doc: Returns a value with its characters, or bytes, in reverse order.

functions.name: FORMAT
functions.doc: Formats values into a string, printf style: `%s` a string, `%d` an integer, `%f` a float, `%t` any value as text.

functions.name: REGEXP_CONTAINS
functions.doc: Whether `value` has a match of the regular expression anywhere in it.

params.name: regexp
params.doc: a regular expression (RE2); a raw string r'...' saves escaping backslashes

functions.name: REGEXP_EXTRACT
functions.doc: Returns the first part of `value` that matches the regular expression, or NULL. With a capturing group, returns what the group matched.

params.name: regexp
params.doc: a regular expression (RE2); a raw string r'...' saves escaping backslashes

params.name: position
params.doc: where to start searching. 1 when left out

params.name: occurrence
params.doc: which match to return. 1 when left out

functions.name: REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL
functions.doc: Returns every part of `value` that matches the regular expression.

params.name: regexp
params.doc: a regular expression (RE2); a raw string r'...' saves escaping backslashes

functions.name: REGEXP_REPLACE
functions.doc: Replaces every match of the regular expression. In `replacement`, `\1` is what the first group matched.

params.name: regexp
params.doc: a regular expression (RE2); a raw string r'...' saves escaping backslashes

functions.name: COUNT
functions.doc: Counts the rows, or the rows where the expression is not NULL.

params.name: expression
params.doc: `*` counts every row

notes: Takes `DISTINCT` before the expression to count each value once.

functions.name: COUNTIF
functions.doc: Counts the rows where the condition is TRUE.

example.result: the number of rows with an amount over 100

functions.name: SUM
functions.doc: Returns the sum of the values that are not NULL, or NULL if there are none.
notes: Takes `DISTINCT` before the expression to add each value once.

functions.name: AVG
functions.doc: Returns the average of the values that are not NULL.

functions.name: MIN
functions.doc: Returns the smallest value that is not NULL.

functions.name: MAX
functions.doc: Returns the largest value that is not NULL.

functions.name: MAX_BY
functions.doc: Returns the value of `x` on the row where `y` is largest.

params.name: x
params.doc: the value to return

params.name: y
params.doc: the value to compare

functions.name: MIN_BY
functions.doc: Returns the value of `x` on the row where `y` is smallest.

params.name: x
params.doc: the value to return

params.name: y
params.doc: the value to compare

functions.name: ANY_VALUE
functions.doc: Returns the expression for some row of the group, chosen by BigQuery. NULL only if every row has NULL.

functions.name: ARRAY_AGG
functions.doc: Collects the values of a group into an array.
notes: Also takes `DISTINCT`, `IGNORE NULLS` (it fails on a NULL otherwise), `ORDER BY key` and `LIMIT n` inside the parentheses.

functions.name: STRING_AGG
functions.doc: Joins the values of a group into one string.

params.name: delimiter
params.doc: ',' when left out

notes: Also takes `DISTINCT`, `ORDER BY key` and `LIMIT n` inside the parentheses.

functions.name: LOGICAL_AND
functions.doc: Whether the condition is TRUE for every row where it is not NULL.

functions.name: LOGICAL_OR
functions.doc: Whether the condition is TRUE for at least one row.

functions.name: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT
functions.doc: Estimates the number of different values: faster and cheaper than COUNT(DISTINCT ...) on many rows.

functions.name: APPROX_QUANTILES
functions.doc: Estimates the boundaries of `number` equal groups of the values: `number + 1` values, from the minimum to the maximum.

params.name: number
params.doc: how many groups; 100 gives percentiles

functions.name: ROW_NUMBER
functions.doc: Numbers the rows of each partition 1, 2, 3, ... in the order of ORDER BY, with no ties.
notes: Keep the latest row of each key with `QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY key ORDER BY updated_at DESC) = 1`.

functions.name: RANK
functions.doc: Ranks the rows of each partition; ties get the same rank and leave a gap (1, 1, 3).

functions.name: DENSE_RANK
functions.doc: Ranks the rows of each partition; ties get the same rank and leave no gap (1, 1, 2).

functions.name: PERCENT_RANK
functions.doc: Returns the rank of the row in its partition as a fraction from 0 to 1.

functions.name: NTILE
functions.doc: Splits the rows of each partition into `n` buckets as equal as can be, and returns the bucket of the row, from 1.

params.name: n
params.doc: a constant

functions.name: LAG
functions.doc: Returns the value from a row before the current one in the partition.

params.name: offset
params.doc: how many rows back. 1 when left out

params.name: default
params.doc: returned when there is no such row. NULL when left out

functions.name: LEAD
functions.doc: Returns the value from a row after the current one in the partition.

params.name: offset
params.doc: how many rows on. 1 when left out

params.name: default
params.doc: returned when there is no such row. NULL when left out

functions.name: FIRST_VALUE
functions.doc: Returns the value on the first row of the window frame.
notes: Takes `IGNORE NULLS` after the value to skip NULLs.
With ORDER BY, the default window frame ends at the current row: add `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING` to look at the whole partition.

functions.name: LAST_VALUE
functions.doc: Returns the value on the last row of the window frame.
notes: Takes `IGNORE NULLS` after the value to skip NULLs.
With ORDER BY, the default window frame ends at the current row: add `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING` to look at the whole partition.

functions.name: NTH_VALUE
functions.doc: Returns the value on the `n`th row of the window frame, from 1.
notes: With ORDER BY, the default window frame ends at the current row: add `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING` to look at the whole partition.

functions.name: PERCENTILE_CONT
functions.doc: Returns the given percentile of the values in the partition, interpolating between rows.

params.name: percentile
params.doc: from 0 to 1; 0.5 is the median

notes: Its OVER clause takes PARTITION BY only, no ORDER BY.

functions.name: IF
functions.doc: Returns `true_result` if the condition is TRUE, else `else_result`.

params.name: else_result
params.doc: the same type as true_result

functions.name: IFNULL
functions.doc: Returns `expr`, or `null_result` when `expr` is NULL.

params.name: null_result
params.doc: the same type as expr

functions.name: COALESCE
functions.doc: Returns the first argument that is not NULL.

params.name: expr
params.doc: the same type as the others

example.result: the first of them that is set

functions.name: NULLIF
functions.doc: Returns NULL if `expr` equals `expr_to_match`, else `expr`.

example.result: NULL instead of an error when count is 0

functions.name: CAST
functions.doc: Converts a value to another type. Fails the query when it cannot; SAFE_CAST returns NULL instead.

params.name: type
params.doc: e.g. INT64, STRING, DATE, ARRAY<STRING>

params.name: format
params.doc: how to read or write a string, e.g. 'YYYY-MM-DD'

functions.name: SAFE_CAST
functions.doc: Converts a value to another type, or returns NULL when it cannot.

params.name: type
params.doc: e.g. INT64, STRING, DATE, ARRAY<STRING>

params.name: format
params.doc: how to read or write a string, e.g. 'YYYY-MM-DD'

functions.name: JSON_VALUE
functions.doc: Returns the scalar value at a JSON path as a STRING, without quotes. NULL for an object or an array.

params.name: json_path
params.doc: a JSONPath such as '$.user.name'. '$' when left out

functions.name: JSON_QUERY
functions.doc: Returns the JSON value at a JSON path: an object, an array or a scalar, as JSON text.

params.name: json_path
params.doc: a JSONPath such as '$.items[0]'

functions.name: JSON_EXTRACT
functions.doc: Returns the JSON value at a JSON path. JSON_QUERY is its newer name.

params.name: json_path
params.doc: a JSONPath such as '$.items[0]'

functions.name: JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR
functions.doc: Returns the scalar value at a JSON path as a STRING. JSON_VALUE is its newer name.

params.name: json_path
params.doc: a JSONPath such as '$.user.name'. '$' when left out

functions.name: JSON_QUERY_ARRAY
functions.doc: Returns the JSON array at a JSON path as an ARRAY of its elements.

params.name: json_path
params.doc: a JSONPath such as '$.items'. '$' when left out

functions.name: JSON_VALUE_ARRAY
functions.doc: Returns the JSON array of scalars at a JSON path as an ARRAY<STRING>.

params.name: json_path
params.doc: a JSONPath such as '$.tags'. '$' when left out

functions.name: PARSE_JSON
functions.doc: Reads a JSON string as a JSON value.

functions.name: TO_JSON_STRING
functions.doc: Returns any value as JSON text.

params.name: pretty_print
params.doc: TRUE adds line breaks and indents. FALSE when left out

functions.name: ARRAY_LENGTH
functions.doc: Returns the number of elements of an array, or NULL for a NULL array.

functions.name: ARRAY_TO_STRING
functions.doc: Joins the elements of an array of strings with a delimiter.

params.name: null_text
params.doc: put in place of a NULL element. NULL elements are left out when left out

functions.name: ARRAY_CONCAT
functions.doc: Joins arrays of the same element type into one.

functions.name: ARRAY_REVERSE
functions.doc: Returns the array with its elements in reverse order.

functions.name: GENERATE_ARRAY
functions.doc: Returns an array of numbers from `start` to `end`, both included, `step` apart.

params.name: step
params.doc: 1 when left out

functions.name: SAFE_DIVIDE
functions.doc: Divides `X` by `Y`, like `X / Y`, but returns NULL instead of failing when `Y` is 0.

params.name: X
params.doc: the dividend

params.name: Y
params.doc: the divisor

functions.name: ROUND
functions.doc: Rounds `X` to `N` decimal places; halfway cases round away from zero.

params.name: N
params.doc: decimal places; negative rounds to tens, hundreds, ... 0 when left out

params.name: rounding_mode
params.doc: for NUMERIC and BIGNUMERIC only

functions.name: TRUNC
functions.doc: Drops the decimal places of `X` beyond `N`, rounding toward zero.

params.name: N
params.doc: decimal places. 0 when left out

functions.name: ABS
functions.doc: Returns the absolute value of `X`.

functions.name: CEIL
functions.doc: Returns the smallest whole number not less than `X`.

functions.name: FLOOR
functions.doc: Returns the largest whole number not greater than `X`.

functions.name: MOD
functions.doc: Returns the remainder of `X` divided by `Y`, with the sign of `X`.

functions.name: DIV
functions.doc: Divides `X` by `Y` and returns the whole part, rounding toward zero.

functions.name: POW
functions.doc: Returns `X` raised to the power `Y`.

functions.name: SQRT
functions.doc: Returns the square root of `X`.

functions.name: LOG
functions.doc: Returns the logarithm of `X` to base `Y`, or the natural logarithm with no `Y`.

params.name: Y
params.doc: the base; e when left out

functions.name: GREATEST
functions.doc: Returns the largest of the arguments; NULL if any of them is NULL.

functions.name: LEAST
functions.doc: Returns the smallest of the arguments; NULL if any of them is NULL.

functions.name: RAND
functions.doc: Returns a random number from 0 (included) to 1 (not included).

functions.name: GENERATE_UUID
functions.doc: Returns a random UUID as a STRING of 36 characters.

functions.name: FARM_FINGERPRINT
functions.doc: Returns a stable INT64 hash of a value, the same on every run.

example.result: a stable bucket from 0 to 9 for each user
